1_placement_churn_is_the_real_healing_co.detail: the re-form RE-TILES every range instead of pinning survivors to what they already hold. After the second kill: a survivor moved [10:22)->[39:51), another [46:51)->[22:27), another [34:46)->[10:22). Three UNTOUCHED nodes each had to download ~25GB before the ring could serve.
1_placement_churn_is_the_real_healing_co.consequence: one node death costs ~29 minutes of ring downtime even though the replacement node was ready in ~12 seconds
1_placement_churn_is_the_real_healing_co.fix_shape: make placement prefer the assignment that maximises cached-range reuse across surviving stages (a stickiness term in shard.plan). Would turn a ~29min outage into a ~1-2min one.
1_placement_churn_is_the_real_healing_co.evidence: both heals in this receipt: 1739s and 1826s ring downtime vs 12s warm-node readiness

2_churn_returns_a_truncated_completion_a.detail: when the tail was killed mid-stream, the gateway returned HTTP 200 with a partial answer and finish_reason 'stop'. A caller cannot distinguish this from a genuine completion.
2_churn_returns_a_truncated_completion_a.consequence: settlement correctly refuses to pay, so the operator is not charged — but a paying user silently receives a short answer
2_churn_returns_a_truncated_completion_a.fix_shape: surface an error (or transparently retry on the healed ring) instead of presenting a truncated stream as a normal stop

3_no_perf_metrics_on_the_serve_path.detail: SHARD_JOB_DONE carries only jobId/ok/tokensGenerated/receiptsOk/nonce/degraded — no tok_s, ttft_ms or transport split, so this ring produced no interactive-speed numbers
3_no_perf_metrics_on_the_serve_path.note: PR #133 added serve perf metrics; they are not present in this payload — worth re-checking whether they are emitted elsewhere or regressed
